#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR fixes a failing storage e2e test and generally improves the maintainability of this code path. 

The existing implementation is prone to race conditions and flakes quite often. Specifically, the following is problematic: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/005f184ab631e52195ed6d129969ff3914d51c98/test/e2e/storage/pvc_storageclass.go#L68-L70 the test should unset default StorageClasses *before* creating a PVC/PV. However, the existing logic is incorrectly under a `defer` and this results in a default StorageClass being available at a point in time where the test expects there to be no default StorageClasses.

See the linked issue for more context.

@dims I reviewed the test as I added it some time ago (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/f765e191d19bc8029e3951fd307ff024a83fb2e2) but did not see any obvious issue with the test.

Furthermore I've ran the test on GCP kOps cluster to see if I would be able to reproduce the issue and could not, unless running this during the test: `while true; do oc patch sc/balanced-csi -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"true"}}}';done`

So I was thinking: since this is a serial (and disruptive) test, if it's really running serially - but looking at the `e2e-ci-kubernetes-e2e-cos-gce-serial-canary` job it does not have `max_concurrency: 1` parameter, maybe it should? I don't know much about Prow, but it seems like without this there is no guarantee the test will be isolated/serial?

Similarly the `e2e-ci-kubernetes-e2e-al2023-aws-serial-canary` serial tests are failing too and also miss this parameter.

It definitely looks like a test running in parallel messing things up here at first glance, but the test is tagged with [framework.WithSerial()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4bc6a11d78b0506bf7c20b71c9e12e695bcab737/test/e2e/storage/pvc_storageclass.go#L65) and Ginkgo itself ensures that serial tests run sequentially - so thats not it, also see job [log](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/e2e-ci-kubernetes-e2e-cos-gce-serial-canary/1825752444232011776/build-log.txt):

```
kubetest2 kops \
...
  --parallel=1
```
----

Taking a closer look, it seems that the test logic as written is quite brittle. Specifically, the fact that untagging existing default StorageClasses is under a defer statement: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4bc6a11d78b0506bf7c20b71c9e12e695bcab737/test/e2e/storage/pvc_storageclass.go#L69-L70

I would expect this logic to be executed first, not after the test function completes and is invoked by the defer.

Can we simplify things here? the core behavior of the feature as I understand it is _assigning a default StorageClass to a PVC that was created without one_. 

The test cluster should already have a default StorageClass (If we want to ensure this, we could add a step at the beginning to check for a default SC or create one if none exists), so all that we really need to do is:

1. Create a PVC with `StorageClassName` explicitly set to `nil`.
2. Wait for the PVC to be bound.
3. Verify that the bound PVC has a StorageClass assigned.

that should give us the needful code coverage and we can remove untagging at first, creating a StorageClass later, and so on which is prone to race conditions.

review_comments:
How exactly does this change help with **suspected** race with other tests? It still relies on modifying existing storage classes for the duration of the test, and also reverts SC settings via `defer`. The only thing changing is that here we don't check for specific storage class name being assigned to PVC making the test even less predictable as it would tolerate any SC being assigned - which should never happen during execution of this test. Seems like we're masking the problem without knowing the root cause.

If this test is serial and disruptive, how is it possible that it seems to be racy? Did we rule out the Prow config?

Thank you for the review Roman! The latest revision now validates the StorageClass assignment as well.

> If this test is serial and disruptive, how is it possible that it seems to be racy? Did we rule out the Prow config?

The following logs can be observed in every failure:
```
0820 06:06:25.981634 15020 pvc_storageclass.go:178] PersistentVolumeClaim retro-pvc-lmzlm has unexpected StorageClass balanced-csi, expected StorageClass is: retromr8np
```

`balanced-csi` StorageClass is created by kOps during bootstrap. I believe we should be able to disable this via the `ManageStorageClasses` [parameter](https://github.com/kubernetes/kops/blob/e7be8333165b5494b00a9de634c5d687ae67daab/pkg/apis/kops/componentconfig.go#L931). Doing this, there should be no need to unset default storage classes in the test itself. 

We can either go with that approach, or introduce additional validation in the test here to address this race. As I understand the issue, it is possible for the [StorageClass lister ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b2031b3cb46e946ee72eab7bda87b046db138d62/plugin/pkg/admission/storage/storageclass/setdefault/admission.go#L108)to return cached data if the PVC gets created immediately after the SC label has been updated.

Would love to hear your thoughts on this.

I don't know much about kOps but was suspecting it of reconciling the `balanced-csi` storage class - but so far I could not find it and it seems like it's a one off action - and if it is then introducing additional validation would reveal it (test should timeout and fail if it can't ensure no SCs are default). I think this should be done anyway as it makes the test more robust.

Disabling the SC with `ManageStorageClasses` seems like a pretty good idea and I think you're right, in that case we should get a cluster with no default SCs, but relying on that in the test does not seem right. If somehow it would get re-enabled in the future, the failures would be reintroduced. Also, this might break other test, maybe some of them already rely on having a default SC :shrug:

So I'd first try the additional validation, and if the test starts failing due to SC being periodically reconciled go with disabling `ManageStorageClasses`. WDYT?
